title: DCTS: Differentiable Clock Tree Synthesis Based on Probabilistic Graphical Model
evidence_span: DCTS re-parameterizes discrete clock-tree topology search as a continuous gradient-based problem with a probabilistic graphical model, jointly co-optimizing topology and buffer sizing. On ISCAS'89 and OpenCores circuits at ASAP7 it reports competitive commercial-tool PPA, 2.78x speedup on large circuits, at least 20% delay, 17% skew, 1% power, and 17% area improvement over academic solutions, plus 1.98x minimum speedup.
problem: Traditional CTS splits clustering, topology generation, and buffering into sequential stages that can become trapped in local optima; differentiable methods struggle with dynamic topology changes.
method_or_artifact: End-to-end differentiable CTS using a probabilistic graphical model to represent discrete topology search continuously and co-optimize topology with buffer sizing.
workload_or_benchmark: ISCAS'89 and OpenCores benchmark circuits under the ASAP7 technology node; large-scale circuit timing/power/area evaluation.
hardware_or_process_assumptions: ASAP7 technology-node physical-design flow and clock-tree synthesis objectives; commercial-tool comparison conditions are not fully exposed.
limits: The official description does not provide circuit-by-circuit results, clock-tree constraints, convergence behavior, or commercial-tool configuration; independent paper-level verification remains required.

title: Paretopilot: Global Optimization Reasoning on HLS Design Space Exploration with LLMs
evidence_span: ParetoPilot uses a dedicated LLM to navigate combinatorial HLS directive spaces with global-optimization reasoning, directive scheduling, and quality awareness. It reports 49.5% better DSE performance and 1.8x efficiency over a state-of-the-art heuristic method, and 81.4% improvement over DeepSeek-R1.
problem: The combinatorial explosion of HLS directives makes it difficult for heuristic search to find Pareto-optimal designs under tight budgets.
method_or_artifact: LLM-guided HLS design-space exploration using global optimization reasoning, directive scheduling, and quality-aware Pareto-front shaping.
workload_or_benchmark: HLS directive/configuration design spaces evaluated by Pareto-front quality and search efficiency.
limits: The description does not disclose prompt/interface design, model size, benchmark suite, search budget, or how Pareto quality is measured; LLM claims require paper-level reproducibility review.

title: MBA: Mega-Buffer Architecture Based on 1T1C IGZO eDRAM for Efficient LLM Inference
evidence_span: MBA integrates gigabyte-scale on-chip 1T1C IGZO eDRAM buffers with KV-cache-prioritized mapping, double buffering, and iteration-aware eviction to reduce HBM traffic and sustain compute utilization. It reports 5.99x and 3.63x end-to-end speedups and 8.86x and 4.93x energy-efficiency improvements against GPU and LLM-accelerator baselines.
problem: Weight and KV-cache transfers between GPU and HBM constrain LLM inference; compression can reduce traffic but may be task-specific or harm accuracy.
method_or_artifact: Mega-buffer architecture using IGZO eDRAM, KV-cache prioritized mapping, double-buffered pipelines, and iteration-aware eviction/data reuse.
workload_or_benchmark: LLM inference with substantial weight and KV-cache traffic; GPU and dedicated LLM-accelerator comparisons.
hardware_or_process_assumptions: Gigabyte-scale on-chip 1T1C IGZO eDRAM integrated with an accelerator; density, retention, endurance, fabrication, and area assumptions require verification.
limits: The description does not identify LLMs, sequence lengths, eDRAM technology assumptions, area cost, accuracy effects, or exact baseline configurations.

title: AHASD: Asynchronous Heterogeneous Architecture for LLM Adaptive Drafting Speculative Decoding on Mobile Devices
evidence_span: AHASD decouples draft-model execution on PIM from target-model verification on an NPU, using entropy-history-aware drafting control, time-aware pre-verification, attention units, and gated task scheduling in LPDDR5-PIM. Across LLMs and adaptive drafting algorithms it reports up to 4.2x throughput and 5.6x energy-efficiency gains over GPU-only, 1.5x throughput and 1.24x energy-efficiency gains over GPU+PIM, with under 3% DRAM-area overhead.
problem: Adaptive speculative decoding on a mobile single-NPU-PIM system suffers from idle time under synchronous execution and wasted work under asynchronous execution when draft lengths fluctuate.
method_or_artifact: Task-level asynchronous heterogeneous NPU-PIM architecture with DLM/TLM decoupling, entropy-history-aware control, time-aware pre-verification, localized attention, and gated task scheduling.
workload_or_benchmark: Multiple LLMs and adaptive speculative-decoding algorithms on a mobile LPDDR5-PIM/NPU system.
hardware_or_process_assumptions: Single-NPU mobile system with LPDDR5-PIM, attention units, and sub-microsecond task switching; DRAM-area overhead below 3% is reported.
limits: The description does not expose model sizes, acceptance rates, thermal/area methodology, absolute latency, or adaptive-draft distributions; cross-device generalization remains unverified.

title: Legotherm: Modular and Reusable Thermal Model for Chiplet-Based Heterogeneous Integration
evidence_span: LegoTherm decomposes chiplet systems into reusable reduced-order thermal components, constructs high-fidelity 3D meshes with micro-interconnection detail, and aggregates thermally coupled interface ports for rapid reassembly. On industrial-scale 2.5D and 3D packaging benchmarks it reports up to 10.39x speedup over COMSOL with mean relative error below 0.40%, reducing design iterations from weeks to half a day.
problem: Hundreds of thermal simulations across power, cooling, and structural scenarios make FEM and compact thermal models too inflexible or expensive for complex chiplet stacks.
method_or_artifact: Modular discretization and reduced-order thermal modules with interface-port aggregation, preserving hotspot accuracy while allowing rapid scenario reassembly.
workload_or_benchmark: Industrial-scale 2.5D and 3D heterogeneous-packaging thermal benchmarks with varying power distributions, cooling conditions, and stack structures.
hardware_or_process_assumptions: Chiplet-based 2.5D/3D integration with cross-scale micro-interconnects and thermal coupling; industrial benchmark details are not public in the description.
metrics: design iteration time from weeks to half a day
limits: The official description does not give mesh sizes, calibration data, absolute runtimes, cooling conditions, or error distributions across scenarios.

title: REFLEX: Rewrite-Free Row-Aligned Sparse Attention for Efficient LLM Execution on PIM
evidence_span: REFLEX co-locates required KV-cache entries in a single DRAM row and uses activation-aware scheduling to integrate sparse attention with PIM without rewriting the cache or changing hardware. It reports up to 1.64x throughput and 1.36x energy-efficiency improvement on PIM, plus 1.37x throughput in GPU-PIM systems.
problem: Sparse attention reduces work, but irregular KV-cache accesses span DRAM rows and cause unnecessary activations and cache rewrites when combined naively with PIM.
method_or_artifact: Rewrite-free row-aligned KV placement and activation-aware PIM scheduling for sparse attention, preserving accuracy without hardware changes.
workload_or_benchmark: LLM decoding with sparse attention and KV caches on PIM and GPU-PIM systems.
baselines: PIM sparse-attention execution without row alignment
limits: The description omits model/sequence suites, sparsity patterns, row-mapping overhead, memory technology, and accuracy measurements.

title: STELLAR: Structure-Guided LLM Assertion Retrieval and Generation for Formal Verification
evidence_span: STELLAR represents RTL blocks as AST structural fingerprints, retrieves structurally relevant RTL/SVA pairs from a knowledge base, and injects them into structure-guided prompts for LLM-based SystemVerilog Assertion generation. The evaluation reports superior syntax correctness, stylistic alignment, and functional correctness.
problem: Manual SystemVerilog Assertion writing is slow and error-prone, while existing LLM methods either generate from scratch or ignore structural patterns and expert assertions.
method_or_artifact: Structure-aware retrieval-augmented LLM assertion generation using RTL AST fingerprints and a knowledge base of RTL/SVA pairs.
workload_or_benchmark: RTL blocks and SystemVerilog Assertions for formal-verification flows.
limits: The description provides no numerical results, model details, retrieval corpus size, property coverage, or proof-validity conditions; industrial-flow claims require primary-paper evidence.

title: A Remote Side-Channel Attack on Post-Quantum Key Encapsulation Mechanisms: A Case Study of ML-KEM on Intel x86
evidence_span: The study presents a remote power side-channel attack on a complete standardized ML-KEM implementation on Intel x86. It treats remotely observed power traces as a plaintext-checking oracle and reports secret-key recovery from PQClean with up to 99.5% success, despite speculative execution and dynamic power management.
problem: Remote side-channel resilience of standardized post-quantum cryptography is underexplored, while microarchitectural and power-management mechanisms may still leak secrets.
method_or_artifact: Generic remote power side-channel analysis and secret-key recovery against ML-KEM, using plaintext-checking behavior as an oracle on Intel x86.
workload_or_benchmark: PQClean ML-KEM implementation on a modern Intel x86 processor with remote trace collection.
metrics: effect of speculative execution and dynamic power management
limits: The description does not specify network distance, noise, trace counts, processor SKU, attack time, mitigations, or transfer to other ML-KEM implementations.

title: Early Design Stage Thermal Prediction and Optimization: Machine-Learning Driven Approach
evidence_span: The framework predicts power-density maps during global placement, estimates steady-state temperature through physics-guided thermal interpolation, and uses ML-based placement optimization to reduce hotspots without timing degradation. It reports 49.0% and 34.9% prediction-accuracy improvements over tool estimation and reduces maximum temperature by 9.97 degrees Celsius while maintaining equivalent timing and area.
problem: Advanced-node power density makes thermal effects first-order, but traditional thermal mitigation is inaccurate early or expensive after fabrication/post-route.
method_or_artifact: ML power-density prediction, physics-guided thermal-map interpolation, and ML-driven placement optimization for early thermal mitigation.
workload_or_benchmark: Modern SoC physical-design placement and thermal prediction/optimization; exact circuit suites and technology nodes require paper-level extraction.
limits: The description does not define accuracy metrics, circuits, technology, training data, timing constraints, or transfer across placements; claimed reliability improvements need full-paper validation.

title: Mappingevolve: LLM-Driven Code Evolution for Technology Mapping
evidence_span: MappingEvolve abstracts technology mapping into optimization operators and uses a Planner/Evolver/Evaluator hierarchy to guide LLM-driven code evolution. The official description reports 10.04% area reduction versus ABC, 7.93% versus mockturtle, 46.6%–96.0% S_overall improvement on EPFL benchmarks, explicit area-delay tradeoff navigation, and an open-source framework.
problem: LLMs have been used to generate optimization scripts, but their ability to improve the core technology-mapping algorithm remains underused.
method_or_artifact: Open-source hierarchical agent framework that plans, evolves, and evaluates technology-mapping code through structured optimization operators.
workload_or_benchmark: Technology-mapping experiments on EPFL benchmark circuits with area-delay tradeoff evaluation.
limits: The description does not disclose model/API costs, evolution budgets, reproducibility details, benchmark split, or how code validity and regression risk are controlled.
